mission: Greyline hits the archive as a cleanup team, not a battlefield unit. They seal exits, wipe cameras, trigger old quarantine protocols, and try to leave no clean version of the room behind. Vara Senn appears as an attached Force specialist, making the scene psychologically unsafe. Before taking Iressa hostage, Vara engages Ben in a short, cramped lightsaber clash. Vara/Ben clash beat: Vara fights with blunt Lost Tribe aggression: pressure, fear, domination, and taunts. Ben recognizes elements of Lost Tribe training, allowing a brief Vestara Khai scar-tissue mention. The fight is short, ugly, and consequential, not a grand duel.
why_now: The archive waking confirmed that Greyline was watching the site. The cleanup team’s arrival now — sealing exits, wiping cameras, triggering old quarantine protocols — is a containment operation against the specific discovery Ben and Iressa just made. If they don’t get out with the proof, there is no proof.
conflict: Ben has to hold the archive long enough for Iressa to finish corrupting the data, but Vara Senn’s presence as a Force specialist makes this psychologically as well as physically dangerous. The fight is not a duel — it’s a delay action in a cramped server-room aisle while Greyline seals every exit. Vara recognizes that combat won’t give her control fast enough and changes strategy.
turning_point: Vara senses Iressa has hidden something.
closing_hook: Vara senses Iressa has hidden something.
setting: Coruscant, the decommissioned GAG quarantine archive — narrow rows of cabinet-style data storage, single emergency strip lighting along the floor. Greyline arrives as a cleanup team: they seal exits, wipe cameras, and trigger old quarantine protocols to scrub the site. Vara Senn engages Ben in a cramped, ugly lightsaber clash between cabinet rows. Confined space, no room for grand form.
emotional_trajectory: Vara should be dangerous but not Ben’s true mirror. Ben can handle the fight, but Vara recognizes that combat will not quickly work and changes tactics. This is Pinch Point 1 — the antagonist shows organized lethality. Restraint is about to cost something.

stakes.personal: Ben recognizes elements of Lost Tribe combat training in Vara — pressure, domination, manufactured fear — and feels the old Vestara scar-tissue flare. More uncomfortable: he knows this style and knows how to read it, because Jacen trained him to read Force-pressure before it becomes physical.
stakes.interpersonal: Vara treats Ben as an obstacle worth noting, not a peer worth respecting — she's a crowbar doing contract work. Her contempt for Jedi restraint is theatrical but tactically genuine. Talon reads the room from behind the nearest cabinet row and tracks exits.
stakes.external: Greyline is sealing the archive to leave no clean copy. Iressa is still at the terminal finishing the data corruption. Every second Ben holds Vara is a second Iressa has to complete the transmission. Vara sensing that Iressa has hidden something changes the tactical picture completely.

sensory_details: The emergency strip lighting pulses red when quarantine protocol triggers — the floor-level strips make everything below knee height visible and everything above indeterminate. The cabinet rows are narrow enough that a lightsaber can't be swung freely; the only moves are thrust, redirect, and slam. Vara smells of armor sealant and something chemical Ben associates with the Lost Tribe's particular brand of Force-fear pressure — the sensation arrives before she speaks.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Vara reads Iressa's body language during the clash — the focused stillness of someone completing something despite physical fear — and understands that Iressa is still working, not frozen.
turning_point_detail.shift: Vara abandons the lightsaber fight and pivots to hostage tactics. Greyline doesn't need to win the fight; they need to stop the transmission.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben can win the combat and still lose the moment. Restraint — not attacking aggressively while Vara's attention is on Iressa — is about to have a specific cost.

emotional_arc.start: Ben is alert and operational — fighting defensively in the cramped aisle, protecting Iressa's working time, reading Vara's Lost Tribe patterns.
emotional_arc.shift: The Vestara scar-tissue reflex fires: Ben knows this style and knows how to counter it more aggressively than he's willing to. He chooses restraint. Vara notices.
emotional_arc.end: Vara changes tactics — she senses Iressa has hidden something. The tactical situation has flipped. Ben held the fight; the fight just stopped being the point.

key_beats.beat_description: Greyline arrives as a cleanup unit: exits sealed, cameras wiped, quarantine protocols triggered — the operation is containment, not confrontation.
key_beats.state_change: The archive becomes a sealed room with a countdown — every second Ben holds the aisle is a second Iressa has at the terminal.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The professional read that makes the stomach drop slightly: these people are not improvising.

key_beats.beat_description: Vara Senn engages Ben in the narrow cabinet aisle — thrust, redirect, slam — using Force-pressure and manufactured fear rather than room to maneuver.
key_beats.state_change: The fight is a delay action, not a duel — Ben's defensive posture is the correct call, but it costs him aggression he could spend.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The read of her style arriving as body-knowledge before analysis — a particular registration of pressure that has a specific name he doesn't want to use.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben identifies elements of Lost Tribe training in Vara's patterns; the Vestara scar-tissue reflex fires briefly and he holds his aggression back.
key_beats.state_change: Ben's restraint is visible as restraint — he has room to escalate and doesn't take it.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The held impulse registering as a specific pressure in the hands — not fear, the thing that lives next to fear.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon reads exit geometry from behind the nearest cabinet row while Iressa continues the data corruption at the terminal behind Ben's fighting line.
key_beats.state_change: The defensive perimeter is distributed across three people without coordination — Iressa working, Talon mapping, Ben holding.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The peripheral awareness of the terminal sounds behind him — the particular attention that splits without losing the thread.

key_beats.beat_description: Vara reads Iressa's focused working stillness during the clash and abandons the lightsaber fight to pivot toward hostage tactics.
key_beats.state_change: The tactical frame inverts: Ben held the fight and the fight just stopped being the point.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The moment Vara's attention shifts direction — clocked before fully understood, the decision to recalculate already running.
